title: Globally Harmonized System of Classification and Labelling of Chemicals, Seventh revised edition
sourceKind: UN model system — supporting technical source, not directly binding Canada WHMIS law
legalPrecedence: Canadian Hazardous Products Act and Hazardous Products Regulations (HPR SOR/2015-17) take precedence. Health Canada supplier guidance is interpretive. UN GHS is supporting technical context.
sourceStatus: Identity, contents and selected mixture principles checked. Individual criteria/decision trees NOT yet independently validated against Canadian HPR.

keySources.title: Classification of hazardous substances and mixtures
keySources.use: Data precedence, evidence, mixture classification and expert judgement

keySources.title: Physical hazards
keySources.use: Technical reference for Canadian HPR Part 7; individual Canadian adoption must be checked

keySources.title: Acute toxicity
keySources.use: Inhalation, oral, dermal, ATE estimates, route-specific unknown toxicity

keySources.title: Reproductive toxicity
keySources.use: Mixture cutoffs and effects on or via lactation

keySources.title: Environmental hazards
keySources.use: Do NOT treat as adopted Canadian WHMIS hazard classes

keySources.title: Hazard and precautionary statements and pictograms
keySources.use: Supporting communication text; Canadian label/supplemental rules prevail

keySources.title: SDS guidance
keySources.use: Technical SDS reference; Canadian HPR SDS and bilingual rules prevail

keySources.title: GHS classification example
keySources.use: Illustrative test case, must cross-check Canadian criteria

verifiedPrinciples.summary: Use full-mixture data first, bridging where mixture test data absent, and ingredient method where neither applies.

verifiedPrinciples.summary: Expert judgement and weight of evidence apply to qualitative classifications.

Separate unknown-ingredient disclosure and >10% formula correction.
